paper_title: Evaluating Data Augmentation Techniques for Coffee Leaf Disease
core_problem: The need for efficient and less knowledge-intensive detection and classification of diseases in Robusta coffee leaves, exacerbated by small and imbalanced datasets like RoCoLe.
methodology_summary: Deep learning approaches using the RoCoLe dataset, incorporating pix2pix for segmentation and CycleGAN for data augmentation, and evaluating Transformer-based models alongside online and offline augmentations.
empirical_results: Transformer-based models, online augmentations, and CycleGAN augmentation were shown to be effective in improving leaf disease classification, with synthetic data complementing real data to enhance performance.
explicit_limitations: The job requires extensive botanical knowledge and much wasted time; synthetic data has limitations.
